questions.problem: Given that $a=⟨-2,4,3⟩,$ $b=⟨-1,3,2⟩,$ and $c=⟨2,-1,4⟩,$ find $a\cdot (b\times c)$ using the definition of the scalar triple product.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the cross product:

$$
\begin{aligned}b\times c & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(3\cdot 4-2\cdot (-1))i-((-1)\cdot 4-2\cdot 2)j+((-1)\cdot (-1)-3\cdot 2)k \\  & =14i+8j-5k \\  & =⟨14,8,-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can compute the scalar triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =⟨-2,4,3⟩\cdot ⟨14,8,-5⟩ \\  & =(-2)\cdot 14+4\cdot 8+3\cdot (-5) \\  & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $a=⟨-2,0,-1⟩,$ $b=⟨-2,-1,0⟩,$ and $c=⟨3,1,4⟩,$ find $a\cdot (b\times c)$ using the definition of the scalar triple product.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the cross product:

$$
\begin{aligned}b\times c & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =((-1)\cdot 4-0\cdot 1)i-((-2)\cdot 4-0\cdot 3)j+((-2)\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot 3)k \\  & =-4i+8j+k \\  & =⟨-4,8,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can compute the scalar triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =⟨-2,0,-1⟩\cdot ⟨-4,8,1⟩ \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-4)+0\cdot 8+(-1)\cdot 1 \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Scalar Triple Product Using a Determinant
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that the scalar triple product $a\cdot (b\times c)$ is just the determinant of the matrix whose rows are given by $a,$ $b,$ and $c.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|-3\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(4\cdot 1-0\cdot 1)-3(3\cdot 1-2\cdot 1)+2(3\cdot 0-2\cdot 4) \\  & =4-3-16 \\  & =-15.\end{aligned}
$$
